question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+2y &=-4 \\  -10x-10y &=20 \\  8x+8y &=-16.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 2 & -4 \\ -10 & -10 & 20 \\ 8 & 8 & -16\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 2 & -4 \\ -10 & -10 & 20 \\ 8 & 8 & -16\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & -2 \\ -10 & -10 & 20 \\ 8 & 8 & -16\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+10{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 8 & 8 & -16\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-8){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now  

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y &=-2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$ and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we need to find $x$  in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-y-2 \\  y &=y,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-y-2 \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
